newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian corn prices hold but buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian corn prices hold but buyers sidelined.

text.p: Malaysian corn prices were holding steady this week but buyers were sidelined awaiting consolidation following recent sharp corrections on the Chicago maize market, industry sources said on Tuesday.

Stocks of corn in Malaysia's central region were at about last week's level of 50,000 tonnes. But the impending arrival of 150,000 tonnes by the end of July has made buyers wary of another glut in supply, said traders.
"Buyers know that with such a stock, if they commit to something today, the price could come down tomorrow," said a flour mill official.
Traders said bearish crop projections for U.S. corn has resulted in Chicago maize prices falling sharply in the last week and the Malaysian market should follow suit.
"The price could come down anytime, there's no time frame," said a trader. "If it's holding, it's because sellers aren't meeting buyers' expectations."
Dealers could not give an exact estimate on the price level sought by buyers. Some, however, said sales could pick up with a correction of five to 10 ringgit.
"The price we are selling is already pretty cheap now," said one dealer. "Theoretically, if there is an oversupply, people will just dump at whatever price they get."
"The market should come down by another five to 10 ringgit as the existing stocks will carry forward into August," said another trader.
"But a lot also depends on what happens after August. If there are a lot of people buying and there's not enough cargo the price could shoot up again," he added.
On Tuesday, bulk corn of Chinese origin in Malaysia's central region was quoted at 360-365 ringgit a tonne C&F, unchanged from last week.
Bulk Argentine maize, ex-factories/godowns in the central region, was also steady at 365-370 ringgit.
"A" grade wheat in Malaysia was retained at last week's 690 ringgit a bag. "B" grade wheat was also unchanged at 390 ringgit.
Soymeal prices were also stable at 850 ringgit a tonne for the imported material and 860 for the local stuff.
